nodes.name: Bearing spaces of the pump
aliases: Pump bearing spaces

properties.name: Bearing spaces of the pump
properties.description: Bearing spaces of the pump

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

Entry of air from the outside may cause oil-containing gas to enter the pumping chamber via the rotors seals.

Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. The oil filling levels stated in Figure 4 - which apply to the shutdown (standing still) pump - must be observed. The filling level visible in the oil-sight glass depends on the size of the pump and the type of oil used. If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high, oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and reinstall the plug using a gasket which is in perfect condition. Wipe off any oil residues from the casing. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight.

evidence.text: The bores in the coupling are manufactured to tolerance class H7, the shaft journals of the motor to tolerance class j6 resp. k6. The axial distance L1 (Figure 9) to the flange surface (area M in Figure 6) needs to be maintained according to the table. When not complying with this requirement there exists the likelihood of a mechanical contact and thus the creation of sparks between the coupling halves. Affix the coupling half with the M8 set screw, torque 10 Nm.

properties.name: Coupling star
properties.description: Coupling star

evidence.text: At the pump’s flange the respective studs have been preassembled, the washers and nuts which must be used have been enclosed with the pump. Check to ensure that the touch protection (Figure 7) has been correctly fitted in the pump’s flange. Insert the coupling star into the coupling half on the side of the pump. Align the coupling halves and push the motor on making sure that the flange surfaces run in parallel. Any tilt between motor axis anaxis can give rise to increased wear on the coupling star. Fit washers and nuts, and tighten according to the torque levels given in Figure 10.

nodes.name: DRB pump

properties.name: DRB pump
properties.description: DRB pump

evidence.text: During operation of the DRB, check the oil level and the condition of the oil in the oil level glass and the oiler from time to time. Correct as required (see Sections 6.3 and 6.4). Normally, the oil Tigol 100 is transparent. If it turns dark, this is a sign of early ageing due to excessively high temperatures. Run the DRB pump exclusively under the operating conditions for which it has been designed. Any modification of the operating parameters (e. g. intake pressure, intake temperature, ratio between DRB pump and backing pump) for a longer period may place an inadmissible thermal load on the pump.

Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

nodes.name: Fan cowl

properties.name: Fan cowl
properties.description: Fan cowl

evidence.text: The slits in the fan cowl as well as the fins on the motor and on the pump may be contaminated depending on humidity conditions and the degree of contamination in the ambient air. In order to ensure a sufficient air flow for the motor and the pump’s casing, the grid of the fan cowl must be cleaned with a clean brush when contaminated. Any coarse dirt must be removed from the fins on the motor and the pump.

evidence.text: 6.5 Cleaning the Fan Cowl and the Cooling Fins

A intake screen is located in the intake port to collect foreign objects. It should be kept clean in order to avoid a reduction of the pumping speed. To do so, take off the intake line. nodes.name: Pumping chamber

properties.name: Pumping chamber
properties.description: Pumping chamber

evidence.text: If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and screw the plug back in using a gasket which is in perfect condition. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight. Entry of air from the outside may cause oil-containing gas to enter the pumping chamber via the rotors seals.

Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. The oil filling levels stated in Figure 4 - which apply to the shutdown (standing still) pump - must be observed. The filling level visible in the oil-sight glass depends on the size of the pump and the type of oil used. If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high, oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and reinstall the plug using a gasket which is in perfect condition. Wipe off any oil residues from the casing. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight.
In the presence of a vacuum, the entry of air may cause oil-containing gas to enter the pumping chamber via the rotor seals.

Under dirty operating conditions, contaminants may be deposited in the pumping chamber or on the rotors. After removing the two connecting lines, the contaminants can be blown out with dry compressed air or flushed out with a suitable solvent. Contaminants that cannot be blown or flushed out, can be removed completely from the pumping chamber with a wire brush, metallic sponge or scraper. Then change the oil.

nodes.name: Shaft seal
aliases: Outer shaft seal
Outer shaft sealing ring

properties.name: Shaft seal
properties.description: Shaft seal

evidence.text: Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

When the oil level in the oiler drops and when oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the outer shaft seal is malfunctioning. If the oil loss is only slight, the pump may still be operated for some time, provided the lost oil is topped up regularly. Collect the oil which drips out under the motor. There is the danger that someone may slip. Have the pump repaired.

evidence.text: At the pump’s flange the respective studs have been preassembled, the washers and nuts which must be used have been enclosed with the pump. nodes.name: Change oil in normal operating conditions annually

properties.description: Change oil in normal operating conditions annually
properties.instruction_text: Change oil in normal operating conditions annually

evidence.text:
Operation: Oil change | Meas./
Test quantity:  | Frequency: For normal operating conditions annually When pumping corrosive vapors, in the case of much dust and cyclic operation weekly to quarter yearly | Remark: See Section 6.3.

Before pumping oxygen (or other highly reactive gases) at concentrations exceeding the concentration in the atmosphere (> 21 % for oxygen) it will be necessary to use a special pump. Such a pump will have to be modified and de-greased, and an inert special lubricant (e.g. PFPE) must be used. Very little oil is consumed by wear in the bearings and the gear under clean operating conditions. Under normal operating conditions, change the oil annually. Change the oil more frequently when pumping corrosive vapors or large amounts of dust or when cycling frequently from atmospheric to working pressure.

evidence.text: The oil in the shaft seal housing should be changed every 3,000 operating hours. Unscrew the oil-drain screw under the shaft seal housing, drain out the oil and screw in the oil- drain screw using a gasket which is in perfect condition (see Figure 11). Only use specified oil. Mineral oils and synthetic oils do not mix. Fill in fresh oil at the oiler. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must be visible in the oiler. Maximum level – when the pump is warm = 1/2 of the height of the oiler – when the pump is cold = 1/3 of the height of the oiler. Wipe off any oil residues from the casing.

evidence.text: • Motor coupling half • Coupling star • Nuts and washers When mounting motors for DRB 1000 or DRB 2000, we recommend the use of a lifting device. The motor must be fitted with the pump aligned horizontally. Tilting the pump by over 5° can cause oil to flow from the gear chambers into the pump chamber. All mating surfaces and centering surfaces must be clean, undamaged and free of any paint residues. Only air cooled motors must be used. The fan on the side of the motor is also required to cool the pump housing. If this air cooling arrangement is not present, then the surface temperatures may under certain circumstances exceed the permissible temperature range for the pump (T3, T4).

nodes.name: Repair the pump
aliases: Repair the pump for the faulty inner shaft seal

properties.name: Repair the pump
properties.description: Repair the pump
properties.instruction_text: Repair the pump

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

When the oil level in the oiler drops and when oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the outer shaft seal is malfunctioning. If the oil loss is only slight, the pump may still be operated for some time, provided the lost oil is topped up regularly. Collect the oil which drips out under the motor. There is the danger that someone may slip. Have the pump repaired.

nodes.name: Rewire by interchanging two mains phases

properties.name: Rewire by interchanging two mains phases
properties.description: Rewire by interchanging two mains phases
properties.instruction_text: Rewire by interchanging two mains phases

evidence.text: WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. An arrow on the motor flange shows the correct direction of rotation for the rotor connected to the motor shaft (see Figure 2). To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

If the oil loss is only slight, the pump may still be operated for some time, provided the lost oil is topped up regularly. Collect the oil which drips out under the motor. There is the danger that someone may slip. Have the pump repaired.

evidence.text: • Motor coupling half • Coupling star • Nuts and washers When mounting motors for DRB 1000 or DRB 2000, we recommend the use of a lifting device. The motor must be fitted with the pump aligned horizontally. Tilting the pump by over 5° can cause oil to flow from the gear chambers into the pump chamber. All mating surfaces and centering surfaces must be clean, undamaged and free of any paint residues. Only air cooled motors must be used. The fan on the side of the motor is also required to cool the pump housing. If this air cooling arrangement is not present, then the surface temperatures may under certain circumstances exceed the permissible temperature range for the pump (T3, T4).

nodes.name: Faulty inner shaft seal

properties.name: Faulty inner shaft seal
properties.description: Faulty inner shaft seal

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

properties.description: Loosened deposits remain in the pump

evidence.text: WARNING During cleaning, the rotors must be turned only by hand. Please make sure that the rotors are turned in a way that fingers or hands can not be trapped between the rotors or between rotors and housing. Due to the high mass and inertia of the rotors serious injuries can occur even if the rotors are turned by hand only. The loosened deposits must not remain in the pump. After cleaning, check the pump by slowly turning the rotors by hand. They should move freely and without any resistance. Generally, the DRB pump does not need to be disassembled. If necessary, this should only be done by our after-sales service.

properties.name: Malfunctioning outer shaft seal
properties.description: Malfunctioning outer shaft seal

evidence.text: When the oil level in the oiler drops and when oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the outer shaft seal is malfunctioning. If the oil loss is only slight, the pump may still be operated for some time, provided the lost oil is topped up regularly. Collect the oil which drips out under the motor. There is the danger that someone may slip. Have the pump repaired.

nodes.name: Motor and pump axes tilted rather than aligned

properties.name: Motor and pump axes tilted rather than aligned
properties.description: Motor and pump axes tilted rather than aligned

evidence.text: At the pump’s flange the respective studs have been preassembled, the washers and nuts which must be used have been enclosed with the pump. Check to ensure that the touch protection (Figure 7) has been correctly fitted in the pump’s flange. Insert the coupling star into the coupling half on the side of the pump. Align the coupling halves and push the motor on making sure that the flange surfaces run in parallel. Any tilt between motor axis anaxis can give rise to increased wear on the coupling star. Fit washers and nuts, and tighten according to the torque levels given in Figure 10.

nodes.name: Oil ageing due to excessively high temperatures
aliases: Oil early ageing due to excessively high temperatures

properties.name: Oil ageing due to excessively high temperatures
properties.description: Oil ageing due to excessively high temperatures

evidence.text: During operation of the DRB, check the oil level and the condition of the oil in the oil level glass and the oiler from time to time. Correct as required (see Sections 6.3 and 6.4). Normally, the oil Tigol 100 is transparent. If it turns dark, this is a sign of early ageing due to excessively high temperatures. Run the DRB pump exclusively under the operating conditions for which it has been designed. Any modification of the operating parameters (e. g. intake pressure, intake temperature, ratio between DRB pump and backing pump) for a longer period may place an inadmissible thermal load on the pump.

nodes.name: Oil entering the pumping chamber or pump overheating
aliases: Oil entering pumping chamber or pump overheating
Unspecified cause of oil level too high

properties.name: Oil entering the pumping chamber or pump overheating
properties.description: Oil entering the pumping chamber or pump overheating

evidence.text: If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and screw the plug back in using a gasket which is in perfect condition. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight. Entry of air from the outside may cause oil-containing gas to enter the pumping chamber via the rotors seals.

Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. The oil filling levels stated in Figure 4 - which apply to the shutdown (standing still) pump - must be observed. The filling level visible in the oil-sight glass depends on the size of the pump and the type of oil used. If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high, oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and reinstall the plug using a gasket which is in perfect condition. Wipe off any oil residues from the casing. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight.

Operation: Check oil quality | Meas./

Operation: Check oil quality | Meas./

evidence.text: • Motor coupling half • Coupling star • Nuts and washers When mounting motors for DRB 1000 or DRB 2000, we recommend the use of a lifting device. The motor must be fitted with the pump aligned horizontally. Tilting the pump by over 5° can cause oil to flow from the gear chambers into the pump chamber. nodes.name: Pump turning in the wrong direction
aliases: Unspecified cause of pump turning in the wrong direction

properties.name: Pump turning in the wrong direction
properties.description: Pump turning in the wrong direction

evidence.text: After connecting the motor and every time you alter the wiring, check the direction of rotation.

WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. An arrow on the motor flange shows the correct direction of rotation for the rotor connected to the motor shaft (see Figure 2). To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

evidence.text: 6.7 Cleaning the Pumping Chamber

Under dirty operating conditions, contaminants may be deposited in the pumping chamber or on the rotors. After removing the two connecting lines, the contaminants can be blown out with dry compressed air or flushed out with a suitable solvent. Contaminants that cannot be blown or flushed out, can be removed completely from the pumping chamber with a wire brush, metallic sponge or scraper. Then change the oil.

evidence.text: 6.5 Cleaning the Fan Cowl and the Cooling Fins

The slits in the fan cowl as well as the fins on the motor and on the pump may be contaminated depending on humidity conditions and the degree of contamination in the ambient air. nodes.name: Dropping oil level in the oiler
aliases: Oil level in the oiler drops
The oil level in the oiler drops

properties.name: Dropping oil level in the oiler
properties.description: Dropping oil level in the oiler

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

When the oil level in the oiler drops and when oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the outer shaft seal is malfunctioning. If the oil loss is only slight, the pump may still be operated for some time, provided the lost oil is topped up regularly. Collect the oil which drips out under the motor. There is the danger that someone may slip. Have the pump repaired.

evidence.text: 5.1 Start-up

Check the pump motor’s direction of rotation and the oil level in the oiler and the bearing chambers (see Section 4.2). The DRB can be started together with the backing pump at atmospheric pressure. It is protected against excessively high pressure differentials by a bypass line.

nodes.name: Pump surface temperatures exceed the permissible T3 or T4 range

properties.name: Pump surface temperatures exceed the permissible T3 or T4 range
properties.description: Pump surface temperatures exceed the permissible T3 or T4 range

evidence.text: • Motor coupling half • Coupling star • Nuts and washers When mounting motors for DRB 1000 or DRB 2000, we recommend the use of a lifting device. The motor must be fitted with the pump aligned horizontally. Tilting the pump by over 5° can cause oil to flow from the gear chambers into the pump chamber. All mating surfaces and centering surfaces must be clean, undamaged and free of any paint residues. Only air cooled motors must be used. The fan on the side of the motor is also required to cool the pump housing. If this air cooling arrangement is not present, then the surface temperatures may under certain circumstances exceed the permissible temperature range for the pump (T3, T4).

nodes.name: Pump turning in the wrong direction

properties.name: Pump turning in the wrong direction
properties.description: Pump turning in the wrong direction

evidence.text: After connecting the motor and every time you alter the wiring, check the direction of rotation.

WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. An arrow on the motor flange shows the correct direction of rotation for the rotor connected to the motor shaft (see Figure 2). To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

evidence.text: 6.5 Cleaning the Fan Cowl and the Cooling Fins
6.6 Cleaning the Intake Screen

A intake screen is located in the intake port to collect foreign objects. It should be kept clean in order to avoid a reduction of the pumping speed. To do so, take off the intake line. Remove the dirt trap from the intake flange and rinse it using a suitable solvent. Then thoroughly dry it with compressed air. If the dirt trap is damaged, replace it.

evidence.text:
Operation: Check oil quality | Meas./
Test quantity: Neutralization value (DIN 51 558) | Frequency: For normal operating conditions annually When pumping corrosive vapors, in the case of much dust and cyclic operation weekly to quarter yearly | Remark: If the neutralization value for Tigol 100 is > 2, then an oil change will be required, see Section 6.3.

Under such operating conditions it is recommended to regularly check the neutralization value (to DIN 51 558) based on a sample of oil. If the neutralization value for Tigol 100 exceeds 2, an oil exchange will be required.

nodes.name: Unacceptably high oil level in the bearing spaces

properties.name: Unacceptably high oil level in the bearing spaces
properties.description: Unacceptably high oil level in the bearing spaces

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

notes: one end is not named in the source

evidence.text: If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and screw the plug back in using a gasket which is in perfect condition. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight. Entry of air from the outside may cause oil-containing gas to enter the pumping chamber via the rotors seals.

evidence.text:
Operation: Check oil level | Meas./
Test quantity: Min./max. oil level in oil level glass | Frequency: Before switching on and daily | Remark: Check oil level with the pump at standstill, see Section 4.2.

Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. The oil filling levels stated in Figure 4 - which apply to the shutdown (standing still) pump - must be observed. The filling level visible in the oil-sight glass depends on the size of the pump and the type of oil used. If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high, oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and reinstall the plug using a gasket which is in perfect condition. Wipe off any oil residues from the casing. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight.

conditions.text: If the oil level is too low

notes: one end is not named in the source

evidence.text: The housing for the shaft seal and the oiler are filled with oil when the pump is supplied. The oil level must be visible in the oiler. Correct oil level: 1/3 of the oiler must be filled when the pump is cold. Top up oil as required. The lubricant needed for running the pump is supplied in a separate container. Unscrew the oil-fill plug and add oil. Oil without additives and of viscosity class ISO VG 100 (formerly SAE 30) must be used for the pump. We recommend our special oil Tigol 100. Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. The oil filling levels stated in Figure 4 which apply to switch off pumps (at standstill) must be correctly maintained.

If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Under dirty operating conditions, contaminants may be deposited in the pumping chamber or on the rotors. After removing the two connecting lines, the contaminants can be blown out with dry compressed air or flushed out with a suitable solvent. Contaminants that cannot be blown or flushed out, can be removed completely from the pumping chamber with a wire brush, metallic sponge or scraper. Then change the oil.

evidence.text: WARNING Already small quantities of liquids (from the vacuum chamber or the piping) can lead to liquid damages within the pump. These may lead to a deformation of the rotors and may entirely destroy the pump. Suitable protective measures should be provided as required in the piping on the suction side (separator, T-piece). The pumps are vented with nitrogen. Only remove the packing flanges before immediate connection. If not already done, remove the protective shipping collar flanges from the flanges. We recommend that you retain the transport flanges in case you want to store the pump at a later date. Clean the flanges and check that the sealing surfaces are in perfect condition.

To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

Before pumping oxygen (or other highly reactive gases) at concentrations exceeding the concentration in the atmosphere (> 21 % for oxygen) it will be necessary to use a special pump. Such a pump will have to be modified and de-greased, and an inert special lubricant (e.g. PFPE) must be used. evidence.text: Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. The oil filling levels stated in Figure 4 - which apply to the shutdown (standing still) pump - must be observed. The filling level visible in the oil-sight glass depends on the size of the pump and the type of oil used. If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high, oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and reinstall the plug using a gasket which is in perfect condition. Wipe off any oil residues from the casing. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight.
In the presence of a vacuum, the entry of air may cause oil-containing gas to enter the pumping chamber via the rotor seals.

evidence.text: 6.5 Cleaning the Fan Cowl and the Cooling Fins

The slits in the fan cowl as well as the fins on the motor and on the pump may be contaminated depending on humidity conditions and the degree of contamination in the ambient air. In order to ensure a sufficient air flow for the motor and the pump’s casing, the grid of the fan cowl must be cleaned with a clean brush when contaminated. Any coarse dirt must be removed from the fins on the motor and the pump.

evidence.text:
Operation: Check oil level | Meas./
Test quantity: Min./max. oil level in oil level glass | Frequency: Before switching on and daily | Remark: Check oil level with the pump at standstill, see Section 4.2.

Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. The oil filling levels stated in Figure 4 - which apply to the shutdown (standing still) pump - must be observed. The filling level visible in the oil-sight glass depends on the size of the pump and the type of oil used. If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high, oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and reinstall the plug using a gasket which is in perfect condition. Wipe off any oil residues from the casing. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight.

The oil in the shaft seal housing should be changed every 3,000 operating hours. Unscrew the oil-drain screw under the shaft seal housing, drain out the oil and screw in the oil- drain screw using a gasket which is in perfect condition (see Figure 11). Only use specified oil. Mineral oils and synthetic oils do not mix. Fill in fresh oil at the oiler. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must be visible in the oiler. Maximum level – when the pump is warm = 1/2 of the height of the oiler – when the pump is cold = 1/3 of the height of the oiler. Wipe off any oil residues from the casing.

conditions.text: No oil appears under the shaft seal housing.
No oil appears under the shaft seal housing.

notes: one end is not named in the source

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

When the oil level in the oiler drops and when oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the outer shaft seal is malfunctioning. If the oil loss is only slight, the pump may still be operated for some time, provided the lost oil is topped up regularly. Collect the oil which drips out under the motor. There is the danger that someone may slip. Have the pump repaired.

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

evidence.text: WARNING Already small quantities of liquids (from the vacuum chamber or the piping) can lead to liquid damages within the pump. These may lead to a deformation of the rotors and may entirely destroy the pump. Suitable protective measures should be provided as required in the piping on the suction side (separator, T-piece). The pumps are vented with nitrogen. Only remove the packing flanges before immediate connection. If not already done, remove the protective shipping collar flanges from the flanges. We recommend that you retain the transport flanges in case you want to store the pump at a later date. Clean the flanges and check that the sealing surfaces are in perfect condition.

evidence.text: • Motor coupling half • Coupling star • Nuts and washers When mounting motors for DRB 1000 or DRB 2000, we recommend the use of a lifting device. The motor must be fitted with the pump aligned horizontally. Tilting the pump by over 5° can cause oil to flow from the gear chambers into the pump chamber. All mating surfaces and centering surfaces must be clean, undamaged and free of any paint residues. Only air cooled motors must be used. The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.
